comparator.name: Biology
comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026 programme controls: compulsory 105 + background choice 3 + restricted RO2 6 + minimum RO3 12 + thesis 24 + open 30 = 180 EC framework. No formal major specified. Math A and first-listed laboratory RO2 are illustrative neutral choices. The minimum 12 EC RO3 block remains uninstantiated; two chair-preparing RO3 courses must also be passed, not necessarily exactly two six-credit units. Broader module assumed-knowledge wording does not expressly waive the programme condition. Current chart corroborates credit structure, not chair applicability. Registration and separate zero-credit safety/portfolio obligations preserved. Numerical 180 EC does not certify a complete pathway.
components: General Chemistry for the Life Sciences
The Philosophy and Ethics of Biology

Nine-credit study of invertebrates, algae and fungi combines organismal laboratory work and a field course; its two teaching periods must be completed in order. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety and the zero-credit Biology Skills Portfolio remain separate requirements. The portfolio includes annual reflection and an oral test during the thesis.

Six-credit compulsory study of regression, analysis of variance, categorical data, non-parametric tests and statistical designs, using R. The thesis module’s Ecological Methods alternative does not remove this programme requirement.
Example for entry with VWO Mathematics A: functions, equations, differentiation and integration in Mathematics Applied: Introduction. Students with VWO Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead.

Illustrative restricted option for a cellular, plant or animal direction: laboratory and computational investigation of DNA, RNA and proteins, including cloning, PCR, protein analysis and enzyme kinetics. Other directions use Molecular and Evolutionary Ecology. Final specialisation and thesis preparation remain unverified.

Required 24-credit laboratory, field or data-science/modelling research generating new data, with a plan, scientific article, presentations and defence. Before starting, complete at least 102 prescribed credits including all first-year credits and pass two RO3 courses preparing for the supervising chair. Their current allocation remains unverified. Registration at least one month before starting is mandatory; discuss a project at least four months beforehand.

Choose at least 12 credits from the prescribed RO3 list and pass two RO3 courses preparing for the supervising thesis chair. Some listed courses carry three credits, so the credit minimum and two-course condition must both be met. This reserved block is not a verified combination.
Thirty credits remain open for a minor, individual minor or elective courses.

alternatives.label: Biological sciences: cells, organisms & ecosystems
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule visibly spans molecular and cellular biology, physiology, organisms, evolution, ecology, biodiversity, environmental study, data and research, matching WUR’s cell-to-ecosystem breadth.
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible Biology programme spanning cellular and molecular life, genetics, physiology, organisms, evolution, ecology, biodiversity, laboratory and field methods, statistics.
progression: Current offerings and actual earlier formal prerequisites pass. Life foundations precede dependent biology; mathematical methods precede dependent statistics/data study. Neurobiology has no formal Brain and Behavior prerequisite, so its earlier placement is permitted. PPD is in year one; advanced minimum is met. Retain broad biological priorities and partial organismal/plant coverage.

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular & health biology
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, disease, immunity, neuroscience, laboratory work and data analysis form the visible spine.
alternatives.concept: Concentrates on cell biology, molecular mechanisms, genetics, biochemistry, physiology, microbiology, immunology, disease, neuroscience, laboratory research and biological data analysis.
progression: Current offerings and actual earlier formal prerequisites pass. Brain and Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics; life foundations,cell biology,physiology and biochemistry support advanced health biology. Mathematics and programming precede dependent data study,Machine Learning precedes Deep Learning. The late laboratory course is permitted by actual prerequisites. PPD in year one and advanced minimum pass.
alternatives.distinctness: Different priorities molecular/physiological and neurocognitive mechanisms with biological data analysis have material curricular consequences. Pairwise unique counts 6. Provisional only while external pathway unresolved.

alternatives.label: Ecology, evolution & conservation biology
alternatives.labelReason: Ecology, evolution, biodiversity, conservation, field methods and environmental systems dominate the schedule, with biology foundations retained.
alternatives.concept: Concentrates on biodiversity, ecology, evolution, conservation, organisms, climate, soils, farming, environmental observation and field-based research across changing ecosystems.
progression: Current offerings and actual earlier formal prerequisites pass. Ecology/evolution retain the open curriculum’s actual rules, without invented prerequisite courses. Life foundations precede dependent biology; mathematical/programming foundations precede dependent data study. PPD is in year one; advanced minimum passes. Soil/field/biogeochemical study materially supports ecological questions.
alternatives.distinctness: Different priorities biodiversity, ecosystems, conservation and environmental chemical processes with genetic/physiological foundations have material curricular consequences. Pairwise unique counts 4,10. Provisional only while external pathway unresolved.

core: Cellular, genetic, physiological and organismal biology
Ecology, evolution, biodiversity and organism-environment relationships
Mathematics, statistics, programming and biological data/models
Laboratory and field biological investigation, chemistry and physics
adjacent: Molecular and health applications of biological knowledge
Neural and behavioural mechanisms in organisms
questions: How do biological processes interact across scales?
How can biology improve health and nature?

trace: Importing, cleaning, joining and visualising tabular/spatial data in R and a data research project directly support biological data analysis.
Introduces predictive modelling and machine-learning workflows for complex data.
Adds image analysis relevant to microscopy, anatomy and biological pattern recognition.
Provides neural-network methods for modelling complex biological and biomedical data.
Builds programming foundations useful for biological data analysis and bioinformatics.
Provides mathematical techniques needed for quantitative and computational biological work.
Adds probability, distributions, sampling, estimation and simulation for biological inference.

Tree-of-life diversity, evolutionary roles, organism identification/microscopy/apps, biodiversity measures and a small phylogenetic literature/data project directly support comparative biodiversity investigation. Not identical to a Dutch flora/arthropod field course.

Habitat loss, overharvesting,invasive species,climate threats and conservation planning are studied through a local threatened-species status/protection project and public flyer. Direct conservation reasoning, not an invented independent ecological field experiment.
Studies evolutionary mechanisms from genes to populations and their application across biology.
Covers ecological processes from organisms to ecosystems and introduces ecological modelling.

Oceanography,production,microbial systems,marine habitats and human impacts provide specific ecosystem biology. Seminars/multimedia outreach and description-supported excursions/fieldwork do not guarantee a fixed independent marine experiment or cover all organismal zoology.

Farming systems,biodiversity/environmental impacts,innovation,aquaculture and alternative proteins with a literature-based comparative project implement applied organism-environment questions. Not a dedicated plant-physiology or wet-lab substitution.

Soil field coring,texture/pH/leaching,ICP/IC/SEM and geophysical surveys,Excel data analysis and reports supply concrete abiotic soil/water methods for ecological interpretation. Not plant taxonomy or a generic environmental filler.
Description-supported biosphere-water-rock-atmosphere interactions, system modelling, isotope/proxy analysis and greenhouse-gas fieldwork complement ecosystem-process investigation.
Connects biological systems to nutrient cycles and chemical processes in the environment.
Nutrient cycles, ocean acidification, dynamic environmental models and laboratory biopolymer testing provide a specific environmental chemistry/physics complement to ecosystem biology.
Greenhouse feedbacks, tipping points, ocean acidification and ecosystem/agricultural impacts support biological responses to environmental change; societal response content is complementary.
Develops structure–function reasoning through human anatomy, imaging and anatomical variation.
Applies molecular, cellular and physiological regulation to pharmacology and toxic effects.
Studies microbes, host–pathogen interaction, innate and adaptive immunity and immunopathology.
Relates embryology, anatomy and physiology to mechanisms of disease across organ systems.
Provides comparative neurobiology, animal behaviour, microscopy, anatomy and experimental ethics.
Examines sensory and motor systems connecting neural mechanisms to perception and action.
Extends biological and cognitive analysis to advanced brain functions.

Description-supported evolution of language and animal communication, neural speech mechanisms and hands-on experimental approaches provide a bounded biological cognition contribution; no generic software neural-network equivalence.
Introduces cellular function, genetics, physiology, microorganisms and experimental biological reasoning.

Neural signalling, brain development, learning and combined behavioural/imaging/electrophysiological approaches complement the study of animal behaviour and neurobiology; not a replacement for organismal zoology.
Develops molecular-cell biology, genomes, gene expression, signalling, division, tissues and current research methods.
Examines molecules, cells, tissues, organ systems, homeostasis and organismal physiology.
Covers biomolecules, metabolism, signalling and biochemical foundations of biotechnology and disease.
Provides molecular and microbiological laboratory work, including proteins, PCR, electrophoresis and bioinformatics.
Advances molecular genetics, mutation, inheritance, pathology, testing and treatment.

selection.assessment: Sequentially reconsider broad cells/organisms/ecosystems biology first, then molecular/cellular/health questions and ecological/evolutionary/conservation questions. Their actual6/4/10-course differences implement different biological questions and methods, not an arbitrary floor. Three conditional research trials retained, with formal external route/comparability/final candidate acceptance and stopping uncertified while the chair-preparing RO3 combination remains unresolved. No default three-concept acceptance or academic no-match.

notes.text: The UCR programmes provide related biological study, but do not reproduce all plant and animal specialisms, chemical and physical laboratory sequences or the required 24-credit thesis. Optional UCR research is additional to each 180-credit schedule.

audience.programmeDescription: Study life from cells and genes through organisms, evolution and ecosystems. Wageningen Biology combines biological theory with chemistry, physics, quantitative methods, laboratory and field research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: These UCR directions remain provisional while current thesis preparation for Wageningen Biology is confirmed. The 180-credit external framework is not a certified complete pathway.

curriculum.routeLabel: Common programme with restricted specialisation choices
curriculum.limitation: The listed components reserve 180 credits. The minimum 12-credit RO3 block and its two chair-preparing courses have not been established as a verified combination for a supervising thesis chair. This is a supported credit framework, not a certified complete pathway.

componentNotes.y1-bioorganic: Introduces biomolecular structure, reactivity, stereochemistry, reaction mechanisms and molecular interactions through lectures, exercises and practical work.
componentNotes.y1-ecology1: Introduces ecological theories and principles through research and applications in nature management, agriculture, fisheries and environmental policy.
componentNotes.y1-ecology2: Complements Ecology I with data-generating field, greenhouse or laboratory investigations, a literature-based project proposal, reports and a presentation.
componentNotes.y1-cell: Studies plant, animal and bacterial cells, organelles, cellular organisation, differentiation and communication, with practical investigation and group discussion.
componentNotes.y1-analysis: Develops differentiation, integration and simple first-order differential equations for scientific applications.
componentNotes.y1-chem: Studies molecular interactions, energy exchange, thermodynamics, chemical equilibria, buffers and reaction kinetics in living systems.
componentNotes.y1-genetics: Develops inheritance, chromosome mapping, gene expression, genomics, gene manipulation, population genetics and complex traits.
componentNotes.y1-evolution: Studies evolutionary mechanisms within populations and species, selection, speciation, the history of life and comparative methods.
componentNotes.y1-zoology: Studies vertebrate structure and function, development and evolutionary adaptations through comparative anatomy and laboratory investigation.
componentNotes.y1-plants: Connects plant cells, tissues and whole-plant structure to development, photosynthesis, transport, growth regulation and interactions with microorganisms.
componentNotes.y1-biodiversity: Practises identification of Dutch plants and animals, diagnostic keys, field observations and biodiversity comparisons across habitats.
componentNotes.y1-linear: Applies vectors, matrices, linear systems, eigenvalues, iteration, projection and regression, including numerical software.
componentNotes.y1-stat2: Develops confidence intervals, tests of means, simple linear regression and correlation, checking model assumptions and good statistical practice.
componentNotes.y2-physics: Applies optics, mechanics, fluid flow, diffusion, heat and other physical principles to biological phenomena.
componentNotes.y2-reproduction: Studies plant reproductive strategies, flowering, fertilisation, embryogenesis, seeds and fruits, with practical investigation of structure and development.
componentNotes.y2-physiology: Connects mammalian organ systems, morphology, physiological regulation and environmental adaptation through practical work and a case study.
componentNotes.y2-modelling: Uses mathematical and computational models to turn biological hypotheses into predictions that can be investigated and tested.
componentNotes.y2-microbio: Studies the genetic, physiological, morphological and ecological diversity of microorganisms, supported by practical investigation.
componentNotes.y2-ethics: Examines how biology explains phenomena and informs social, animal, environmental and biotechnology ethics.
componentNotes.y2-development: Studies molecular mechanisms of plant and animal development, including differential gene expression, stem cells, communication and pattern formation.
componentNotes.y2-behaviour: Uses Tinbergen’s four questions to study animal behaviour, with practical data collection and analysis, study design and scientific writing.
componentNotes.y2-diversityskills: Nine-credit study of invertebrates, algae and fungi combines organismal laboratory work and a field course; its two teaching periods must be completed in order. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety and the zero-credit Biology Skills Portfolio remain separate requirements. The portfolio includes annual reflection and an oral test during the thesis.
